news.titleTr: Fed'den faiz artışı sinyali: Bankaların 2027 tahminleri değişti
news.summaryTr: ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması, Fed'in aralık ayında daha güçlü faiz artışına gidebileceği tartışmalarını gündeme taşıdı. Goldman Sachs ve Deutsche Bank faiz artışlarının devamını beklerken, Yardeni Research 50 baz puanlık artış ihtimalini koruyor.
news.articleText: Fed'den faiz artışı sinyali: Bankaların 2027 tahminleri değişti ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması, Fed'in aralık ayında daha güçlü faiz artışına gidebileceği tartışmalarını gündeme taşıdı. Goldman Sachs ve Deutsche Bank faiz artışlarının devamını beklerken, Yardeni Research 50 baz puanlık artış ihtimalini koruyor. ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyon verilerinin beklentilerin üzerinde gelmesi, ABD Merkez Bankasının (Fed) aralık ayında atacağı adımlara ilişkin faiz artışı beklentilerini güçlendirdi. Ekonomistler, faiz artışının büyüklüğü ve sıkılaştırma sürecinin ne kadar devam edeceği konusunda farklı senaryoları öne çıkarıyor. ABD'de tüketici fiyat endeksi (TÜFE) ekimde aylık yüzde 0,4, gıda ve enerji hariç çekirdek TÜFE ise yüzde 0,3 arttı. Her iki gösterge de piyasa beklentilerini 0,1 puan aştı. Verilerin ardından ABD tahvil getirileri yükselirken dolar da değer kazandı. Piyasalarda Fed'in aralık toplantısında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışına gidebileceği ihtimali tartışılmaya başlandı. Daiichi Life: "50 baz puanlık artış beklentisi abartılı" Daiichi Life Research Institute ekonomisti Seiji Katsurahata, enflasyon verilerinin ardından 50 baz puanlık faiz artışı beklentilerinin aşırı olduğunu değerlendirdi. Katsurahata, kısa vadede ABD tahvil getirilerinin yükseliş baskısı altında kalabileceğini, bunun doları desteklerken hisse senedi piyasalarındaki kazanımları sınırlayabileceğini belirtti. Ancak piyasa fiyatlamalarının zamanla 25 baz puanlık artış beklentisinde dengelenmesini bekleyen Katsurahata, böyle bir durumda kısa vadeli tahvil getirilerinin normalleşebileceğini ve doların yükseliş potansiyelinin sınırlanabileceğini ifade etti. Goldman Sachs'tan mart ayında yeni faiz artışı tahmini Goldman Sachs, Fed'in aralık ayında 25 baz puanlık faiz artışı yapacağı yönündeki tahminini korudu. Banka, Mart 2027'de üçüncü bir faiz artışı daha bekliyor. Goldman Sachs ekonomistleri, son iki enflasyon verisinin Fed'in aralık ayında açıklayacağı faiz projeksiyonlarında üçüncü faiz artışına yönelik sinyalleri güçlendirebileceğini belirtti. Banka, faiz artışı döngüsünün sonunda politika faizinin yüzde 4,25-4,50 aralığında zirveye ulaşacağını öngörüyor. Faiz indirimlerinin başlangıcına ilişkin tahminini ise Eylül 2027'den Aralık 2027'ye erteledi. Deutsche Bank da iki faiz artışı bekliyor Deutsche Bank, Fed'in aralık ve Mart 2027 toplantılarında 25'er baz puanlık faiz artırımı yapacağı yönündeki ana senaryosunu korudu. Bankanın "Fed Watcher" raporuna göre, Fed yetkililerinin ekim toplantısı sonrasındaki açıklamalarında şahin tutum devam etti. Yetkililerin enflasyonun yüksek olduğu ve ilave parasal sıkılaştırmanın muhtemelen gerekeceği konusunda büyük ölçüde görüş birliği içinde olduğu belirtildi. Bununla birlikte Deutsche Bank, finansal piyasalardaki oynaklık ve yapay zeka yatırımlarına ilişkin belirsizliklerin Fed'in daha temkinli hareket etmesine neden olabileceğine dikkat çekti. Yardeni Research ise Fed'in aralık ayında 50 baz puanlık faiz artışına gidebileceği beklentisini sürdürüyor. Tahvil getirilerinde yükseliş baskısı sürebilir Capital Economics analisti John Higgins, beklentileri aşan enflasyon verilerinin ABD Hazine tahvili getirileri üzerinde kısa vadeli yükseliş baskısı oluşturabileceğini söyledi. İki yıllık tahvil faizinin 10 yıllık tahvil faizinden daha fazla yükselmesine dikkat çeken Higgins, bu hareketin Fed'in daha sıkı para politikası uygulayacağı beklentisini yansıttığını belirtti. Uzun vadeli tahvil getirilerindeki yükselişin ise büyük ölçüde reel faizler ve vade primindeki değişimlerden kaynaklandığını ifade etti. Capital Economics, hisse senedi piyasalarındaki toparlanmanın kalıcı olmaması halinde tahvil getirilerinin yeniden gerileyebileceğini öngörüyor. Yatırımcılar risk azaltıyor ancak piyasadan çıkmıyor State Street verileri, küresel piyasalarda risk iştahının zayıfladığını ancak yatırımcıların pozisyonlarını tamamen kapatmadığını gösterdi. State Street Risk İştahı Endeksi, ekim ayında üst üste ikinci kez gerileyerek eksi 0,09 seviyesine indi. Kurumsal yatırımcılar döviz ve emtia piyasalarındaki risklerini azaltırken hisse senetleri ve tahvillere yönelik daha olumlu tutumlarını korudu. State Street Markets Hisse Senedi Araştırmaları Başkanı Marija Veitmane, yatırımcıların piyasalardan tamamen çıkmak yerine portföylerinde değişikliğe gittiğini belirtti. Teknoloji hisselerindeki pozisyonların da tamamen kapatılmadığını, yalnızca azaltıldığını ifade etti.

news.title: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts
news.summary: The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase.

news.titleTr: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts
news.summaryTr: The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase.
news.articleText: Bitget Wallet reports sevenfold jump in crypto phishing risk alerts The wallet flagged about 37,000 signing requests a week for phishing in Q3 and said better monitoring likely contributed to the increase. Crypto wallet provider Bitget Wallet said Wednesday it was expanding AI-assisted threat detection after its weekly average of signing requests flagged for potential phishing rose 7.4-fold in the third quarter of 2026. The wallet flagged about 37,000 such requests per week in Q3, up from 5,000 in Q2, according to Bitget Wallet chief operating officer Alvin Kan. “The increase likely reflects both greater threat activity and improved detection capabilities, although the data does not allow us to quantify each factor’s contribution,” Kan told Cointelegraph. The wallet introduced AI-assisted risk detection in Q2, he added. Kan said that the tally counted flagged signing interactions, not unique attacks or confirmed financial losses. Bitget Wallet said its expanded AI checks examine website code and domain registration details for signs of fraud. The wallet also simulates transactions to spot hidden permissions before users sign. Bitget Wallet also said AI helped identify 90% of newly blocked risky domains in October, compared with 36% in Q2. Nearly 70% of domains its AI flagged that month had no matching alerts in the external threat feeds it checked. The findings come amid continued phishing threats targeting crypto users. In July, a trader lost nearly $1 million after signing a malicious Ethereum token approval. An August investigation by Rapid7 uncovered a phishing campaign that targeted 885,000 phone numbers and directed recipients to websites impersonating crypto wallet providers. Related: Phishing, deepfakes, supply chain attacks to fuel 2026’s biggest crypto hacks: CertiK

news.summaryTr: İkinci el otomobil piyasasında ekim ayında ortalama ilan fiyatları yükselirken, enflasyondan arındırılmış reel fiyatlarda düşüş yaşandı. arabam.com'un yayımladığı son veriler, fiyatlardaki değişimin yanı sıra en çok ilana çıkan marka ve modelleri de ortaya koydu.
news.articleText: İkinci el otomobil fiyatlarında şaşırtan tablo: Enflasyon hesabı değiştirdi İkinci el otomobil piyasasında ekim ayında ortalama ilan fiyatları yükselirken, enflasyondan arındırılmış reel fiyatlarda düşüş yaşandı. arabam.com'un yayımladığı son veriler, fiyatlardaki değişimin yanı sıra en çok ilana çıkan marka ve modelleri de ortaya koydu. İkinci el otomobil piyasasında ekim ayına ilişkin fiyat verileri belli oldu. arabam.com'un yayımladığı Aylık Fiyat Endeksi'ne göre, ikinci el araçların ortalama ilan fiyatı bir önceki aya kıyasla sınırlı yükseliş gösterirken, reel fiyatlardaki gerileme devam etti. Eylül ayında 921 bin 307 TL seviyesinde bulunan ortalama ilan fiyatı, ekimde 926 bin 771 TL'ye çıktı. Böylece ikinci el otomobillerin ortalama ilan fiyatında aylık bazda yaklaşık yüzde 0,6 artış yaşandı. Ancak enflasyon etkisi hesaba katıldığında farklı bir tablo ortaya çıktı. Enflasyondan arındırılmış reel fiyatlar, eylül ayına göre yüzde 1,94 geriledi. Bu durum, ilan fiyatlarında nominal artış yaşanmasına rağmen araçların reel değerlerinde düşüş olduğunu gösterdi. İkinci elde en çok bu markalar ilana çıktı Ekim ayında arabam.com platformunda yayımlanan ilanlar incelendiğinde, en fazla ilana sahip otomobil markası Renault oldu. Renault'yu sırasıyla Fiat, Volkswagen, Ford ve Opel takip etti. Hyundai, Peugeot, Toyota, BMW ve Citroen de ilan sayısında ilk 10'a giren diğer markalar arasında yer aldı. Model bazında ise Renault Clio listenin ilk sırasında bulundu. Clio'yu Renault Megane ve Fiat Egea izledi. En fazla ilana çıkan diğer modeller Toyota Corolla, Opel Astra, Ford Focus, Volkswagen Passat, Honda Civic, Volkswagen Polo ve Opel Corsa olarak sıralandı. İlanların yüzde 55'i 1 milyon liranın altında İkinci el otomobil ilanlarının fiyat aralıklarına göre dağılımı, piyasadaki araçların önemli bölümünün 1 milyon TL'nin altında olduğunu ortaya koydu. Ekim ayında 600 bin TL ve altındaki otomobiller toplam ilanların yüzde 29'unu oluştururken, 600 bin 1 TL ile 1 milyon TL arasındaki araçların payı yüzde 26 oldu. Böylece 1 milyon TL ve altındaki araçlar, toplam ilanların yüzde 55'ini oluşturdu. Fiyat aralıklarına göre ilan dağılımı şöyle gerçekleşti: En fazla ilan 10-15 yaşındaki araçlarda Araçların yaş dağılımında ise 10-15 yaş grubundaki otomobiller öne çıktı. Bu gruptaki araçlar toplam ilanların yüzde 30'unu oluşturdu. Beş yaş ve altındaki otomobillerin payı yüzde 27,8 olurken, 6-9 yaş aralığındaki araçların oranı yüzde 16,7 olarak kaydedildi. Daha eski araçlara bakıldığında, 16-20 yaş grubunun ilanlardaki payı yüzde 10,9, 20 yaş ve üzerindeki araçların payı ise yüzde 14,7 oldu. Dizel araçlar ilk sıradaki yerini korudu Yakıt türlerine göre yapılan incelemede, ikinci el otomobil ilanlarında dizel araçların ağırlığı devam etti. Ekim ayında dizel otomobillerin toplam ilanlar içindeki payı, bir önceki aya göre 0,2 puan artarak yüzde 47'ye yükseldi. Benzinli otomobillerin payı ise aynı dönemde 0,2 puan azalarak yüzde 31,2'ye geriledi. LPG'li araçlar yüzde 16,2'lik paya sahip olurken, hibrit otomobillerin oranı yüzde 4,1, elektrikli otomobillerin oranı ise yüzde 1,5 olarak gerçekleşti. Böylece elektrikli ve hibrit otomobillerin toplam ilanlar içindeki payı yüzde 5,6 seviyesinde kaldı. Veriler, ikinci el otomobil ilanlarında dizel ve benzinli araçların ağırlığını koruduğunu, fiyat açısından ise 1 milyon TL ve altındaki otomobillerin öne çıktığını gösterdi.

news.summaryTr: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
news.articleText: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands - Published South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media., external "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December. She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters. The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa". "The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read. "Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon." Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."

Altında kısa vadede 4 bin 150 dolara doğru toparlanma bekleyen Yıldırımtürk, 2027'de ons altının 5 bin doların üzerinde seyredeceğini, gümüşün ise 80 doları görebileceğini söyledi.

news.titleTr: Gram altında 9.500 TL kapıda mı? Yıl sonu için dikkat çeken tahmin
news.summaryTr: İMKUSAD Başkan Yardımcısı Mehmet Ali Yıldırımtürk, altın ve gümüş piyasasına ilişkin beklentilerini paylaştı. Altında kısa vadede 4 bin 150 dolara doğru toparlanma bekleyen Yıldırımtürk, 2027'de ons altının 5 bin doların üzerinde seyredeceğini, gümüşün ise 80 doları görebileceğini söyledi.
news.articleText: Gram altında 9.500 TL kapıda mı? Yıl sonu için dikkat çeken tahmin - İMKUSAD Başkan Yardımcısı Mehmet Ali Yıldırımtürk, gram altında 6.500 TL seviyesinin destek haline geldiğini belirterek yıl sonu için 9.500 TL tahmininde bulundu. - Yıldırımtürk, 2027'de ons altında 5 bin doların üzerinde seyir, gümüşte ise 80 dolar beklentisini paylaştı. İMKUSAD Başkan Yardımcısı Mehmet Ali Yıldırımtürk, CNBC-e canlı yayınında Şafak Tükle'nin sorularını yanıtlayarak altın ve gümüş piyasasındaki beklentilerini değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Altın fiyatlarında ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) faiz politikası ve ekonomik verilerin belirleyici olduğunu söyleyen Yıldırımtürk, yılın ikinci yarısında değerli metalin yükselişinin çeşitli engellerle karşılaştığını ifade etti. ABD'de faiz artırımı beklentilerinin altın üzerinde baskı oluşturduğunu belirten Yıldırımtürk, ons altında 3.870 dolar seviyesinin önemli destek konumunda bulunduğunu söyledi. Ons altının 4.000 dolar üzerinde tutunmaya çalıştığını kaydeden Yıldırımtürk, kısa vadede 4.140-4.150 dolar seviyelerine doğru toparlanma yaşanabileceğini dile getirdi. 2027'de ons altında 5 bin doların üzeri mümkün Altının uzun vadeli görünümünde değişiklik olmadığını belirten Yıldırımtürk, merkez bankalarının rezervlerini çeşitlendirme amacıyla altın alımlarını 2027'de de sürdüreceğini öngördü. ABD'de siyasi belirsizliklerin ve Trump yönetiminin karar alma süreçlerinde yaşanabilecek aksaklıkların altına talebi destekleyebileceğini ifade eden Yıldırımtürk, yapay zekâ yatırımlarına yönelik sorgulamaların da yatırımcı tercihlerinde değişime yol açabileceğini söyledi. Yıldırımtürk, 2027 yılında altının önünde bu yılki kadar fazla engel olmayacağını ve yükselişin kademeli şekilde devam edeceğini belirterek ons altında 5.000 doların üzerinde fiyatlamaların görülebileceğini kaydetti. Gram altında 6.500 TL destek, 9.500 TL hedef Gram altının seyrinde döviz kurunun da etkili olduğunu vurgulayan Yıldırımtürk, yurt içindeki yatırımcı talebinin fiyatları desteklediğini söyledi. Fon krizi sonrasında güvenli liman arayışının öne çıktığını belirten Yıldırımtürk, ons altın uluslararası piyasalarda gerilese bile gram altındaki düşüşün aynı ölçüde gerçekleşmediğine dikkat çekti. Mevduat faizlerinde indirim beklentisiyle vadesi dolan birikimlerin de altına yöneldiğini ifade eden Yıldırımtürk, dolar kurunun yıl sonuna kadar 52-53 TL seviyelerine çıkabileceği beklentisinin gram altın fiyatlarına yansıyabileceğini belirtti. Gram altında 6.500 TL seviyesinin destek haline geldiğini söyleyen Yıldırımtürk, yukarı yönlü hareketlerde 7.000, 7.500 ve 8.000 TL seviyelerinin gündeme gelebileceğini ifade etti. Yıldırımtürk, gram altında yıl sonu kapanışının 9.500 TL seviyesinde gerçekleşmesinin mümkün olduğunu söyledi. 2027 gümüşün yılı olabilir mi? Gümüş piyasasında son dönemde daha sakin bir seyir izlendiğini belirten Yıldırımtürk, endüstriyel metal talebinin önceki döneme göre gündemde daha az yer aldığını ve borsa yatırım fonlarından (ETF) satışlar geldiğini kaydetti. Buna karşın gümüşün enerji ve yapay zekâ alanlarında kullanımının talebi destekleyebileceğini ifade eden Yıldırımtürk, geri dönüşüm oranının altına kıyasla daha düşük olmasının da piyasayı etkileyebileceğini söyledi. Gümüşün 2027'de altınla birlikte yükselişini sürdürebileceğini belirten Yıldırımtürk, kısa vadede 80 dolar seviyesinin görülebileceğini ve mevcut seviyelerin alım fırsatı olarak değerlendirilebileceğini dile getirdi. Altın fiyatlarında Fed'in faiz politikası, merkez bankalarının alımları ve jeopolitik gelişmeler öne çıkarken gram altın üzerinde dolar/TL kuru da belirleyici oluyor. Bu nedenle ons altındaki hareketlerin yanı sıra döviz kurundaki değişim de yurt içi altın fiyatlarının yönünü etkiliyor.

news.title: ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch
news.summary: ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned EU lawmakers that delays in finalizing digital euro legislation could push back its potential 2029 rollout.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch
news.summaryTr: ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned EU lawmakers that delays in finalizing digital euro legislation could push back its potential 2029 rollout.
news.articleText: ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned EU lawmakers that delays in finalizing digital euro legislation could push back its potential 2029 rollout. European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Piero Cipollone called for European Union negotiators to reach a deal on digital euro legislation by year-end to keep a possible 2029 launch on track. Speaking at the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs on Tuesday, Cipollone said adoption of the regulation, part of the EU’s Single Currency Package, would give the ECB the legal certainty it needs to complete preparations. “A delay in adoption could instead postpone the introduction of the digital euro,” Cipollone said, warning that a later launch could deepen Europe’s dependence on foreign payment providers and make it harder for European companies to compete. The ECB aims to be ready for a potential first issuance in 2029 if the EU adopts the regulation this year. Its Governing Council will decide whether and when to issue the digital euro after the legislation passes. The European Parliament’s economic affairs committee approved its position on the digital euro legislation in June in a 43–14 vote. Parliament adopted its negotiating position in July, clearing the way for talks with EU member states. The ECB is preparing a 12-month pilot set to begin in the second half of 2027. Payment providers and selected merchants will test a beta version of the digital euro. The warning comes as the ECB prepares for a leadership change. President Christine Lagarde announced in October that she would step down on Feb. 7, 2027, ahead of the planned pilot. Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027

news.title: Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion
news.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $1.6 billion in November, while stock funds attracted billions of dollars from investors buying the dip.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion
news.summaryTr: US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $1.6 billion in November, while stock funds attracted billions of dollars from investors buying the dip.
news.articleText: Stock ETF buyers pounce on dip as Bitcoin funds bleed $1.6 billion US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $1.6 billion in November, while stock funds attracted billions of dollars from investors buying the dip. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $95 million in net outflows on Tuesday as investors poured billions of dollars into stock funds during a market pullback. Tuesday’s withdrawals brought net outflows from US spot Bitcoin (BTC) ETFs to roughly $1.6 billion since the start of November, according to SoSoValue data. Bitcoin ETF outflows eased for a third straight session, while stock funds accounted for all 17 of the top US-listed ETFs by inflows over five trading sessions, according to Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas. Equity ETF investors “devoured” the dip US-listed ETFs attracted roughly $12 billion per day over those five sessions, with all 17 of the top funds by inflows investing in equities, Balchunas said on X on Tuesday. The biggest beneficiaries included Vanguard’s S&P 500 ETF (VOO), Invesco’s Nasdaq-100 ETF (QQQ) and BlackRock’s iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV). BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $78 million in net withdrawals Tuesday, its eighth straight trading session of outflows. The fund recorded about $1.73 billion in net outflows over the streak, according to Farside Investors. Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin Trust ETF (MSBT) attracted $20 million Tuesday, although the inflows were insufficient to offset broader losses. Bitcoin demand weakens as ETF outflows ease Daily net outflows from Bitcoin ETFs outflows slowed from $430 million Thursday and $412 million Friday to $201 million Monday and $95 million Tuesday, but broader market indicators remained weak, according to CryptoQuant. CryptoQuant’s Bitcoin Bull Score Index dropped to 20 on Monday from 90 on Oct. 13, signaling “extremely bearish” conditions, according to a Tuesday report seen by Cointelegraph. Related: Bitcoin nears 11-week low after ‘discouraging’ US CPI inflation beat The analysts reported that apparent Bitcoin demand contracted by 284,000 BTC over 30 days, the fastest pace since March 2025. CryptoQuant said similar conditions have preceded local market bottoms but warned that a deeper correction remains possible, identifying $73,200 as a key Bitcoin support level. At publishing time, Bitcoin traded at $73,998, down 1% over the past 24 hours, and down 5.2% over the past seven days, according to CoinGecko. news.title: SEC enforcement actions fall 24%, crypto cases in spotlight
news.summary: The SEC filed 348 actions in fiscal 2026, down from 456 a year earlier. Cases included alleged Bitcoin mining fraud and an FTX audit settlement.

news.titleTr: SEC enforcement actions fall 24%, crypto cases in spotlight
news.summaryTr: The SEC filed 348 actions in fiscal 2026, down from 456 a year earlier. Cases included alleged Bitcoin mining fraud and an FTX audit settlement.
news.articleText: SEC enforcement actions fall 24%, crypto cases in spotlight The SEC filed 348 actions in fiscal 2026, down from 456 a year earlier. Cases included alleged Bitcoin mining fraud and an FTX audit settlement. The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filed 348 enforcement actions in fiscal 2026, down 23.7% from 456 a year earlier. Its annual enforcement results included cases involving alleged crypto fraud and failures in FTX’s audits. In its Tuesday release, the SEC said it had charged three purported crypto trading platforms and four investment clubs in an alleged scheme that defrauded investors of at least $14 million. In a separate case, the agency accused the founder of a Bitcoin mining business of misappropriating $48.5 million after raising more than $95.6 million from about 6,400 investors. In April, the SEC settled charges against Francis Decker, the Prager Metis partner who led FTX’s audits, over failures to meet professional auditing standards. In February, a jury found Ismael Zarco Sanchez liable for securities fraud and registration violations over his role in the $300 million CryptoFX Ponzi scheme. In July, a court ordered Michael Noble to pay $1.07 million in a case over his role promoting BitConnect’s crypto lending program. news.title: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
news.summary: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.

news.titleTr: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
news.summaryTr: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
news.articleText: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets - Published Traditional games, squishies and building sets are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show. The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK. The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana. The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10. Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults". The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves. This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year. But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far. Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular. "Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said. Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices. A BBC investigation found an AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question. Meanwhile, debate has intensified about keeping youngsters free from smartphones during the school day. One in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family. Paul Reader, who chairs the Dream Toys selection panel of retailers and experts across the sector, said that parents wanted to engage with their children's play. "Nothing beats a board game with that. Nothing beats a bit of interaction," he said. 'Shop around but check safety' The panel he chairs has selected a list of toys that retailers believe will be some of the most popular this year. It includes variations on popular toys of recent years, including slime, a soft tiger that roars and grows, and a shark that breaks out of an egg. Symonds said that, despite rising sales in the year so far, nearly half of toy sales came in the build-up to Christmas, and families were still looking closely at costs. There was significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10, she said. Reader also urged anyone looking for a bargain to shop around, but to ensure that toys were bought from reputable traders so they were genuine and safe. news.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang. It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman. - Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published12 hours ago Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. What investigations are now under way? Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe. The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC. Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. Huang bet on AI at a time when "there were no customers for the stuff he was building", Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure like Amazon, Google and Microsoft now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. For now, the firm's board appears unlikely to remove Jensen Huang, saying on Sunday they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles. Who is Jensen Huang's wife? Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners. They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer. In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn. Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney - Published21 September

news.title: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia
news.summary: US general warns the Sahel model-like security deal with Russia could lead to greater instability in Africa.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia
news.summaryTr: US general warns the Sahel model-like security deal with Russia could lead to greater instability in Africa.
news.articleText: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia - Published The US has warned Madagascar against strengthening its ties with Russia, saying similar partnerships with military-led governments in West Africa have failed to improve security. US Africa Command deputy head Lt Gen John Brennan said Madagascar's strategic location in the Indian Ocean made it important to global trade. He warned against what he called the "Sahel model", which he said risked fuelling instability across the continent. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, all under military rule, have reduced ties with the Western partners and turned to Russia to support their fight against jihadist groups. Russia has expanded its co-operation with Madagascar since the army seized power in 2025, supplying weapons and military instructors. "We are concerned about Russia wanting to proliferate [the Sahel model] elsewhere across the continent," Brennan told reporters in an online briefing. "Madagascar sits in a location that is extremely important, as is Mozambique, and we don't want to see those models be applied in those two locations," he said. The three Sahel countries had blamed their former Western partners for failing to contain jihadist violence before turning to Moscow. However, Islamist militant attacks have continued despite their closer military ties with Russia. Brennan also raised concerns about security in the Mozambique Channel, which separates Mozambique and Madagascar from mainland Africa and is an important route for international shipping and trade. He said it was vital to prevent militants linked to the Islamist State group in northern Mozambique and other hostile actors from threatening maritime activity. Citing recent piracy-related incidents along the coast, Brennan said they were adapting their tactics, including developing greater maritime capabilities. He said US partners were "free to partner with whom they wish" but urged them to understand the potential risks. Madagascar has not publicly responded to Brennan's comments. However, President Michaël Randrianirina has recently reiterated his support for stronger ties between Russia and African countries. During the Russia-Africa summit last month, Madagascar and Russia signed several co-operation agreements covering defence, tourism and trade. In February, a few months after seizing power, Randrianirina visited to Moscow. It was the first official visit to Russia by a Malagasy leader in nearly 50 years. news.articleText: Electricity bills to rise by 2.5% from March - Published Electricity bills will go up by 2.5% in Jersey from March 2027, it has been announced. Jersey Electricity said the tariff increase would add just over £1 per week for a typical all-electric home from March 2027. The annual rate of inflation in Jersey rose to 3% in September, according to the latest figures. Chief executive Chris Ambler said: "We know that any increase in household costs is unwelcome, so we have worked hard to keep this rise below the island's current rate of inflation." Ambler said: "We have again delayed the increase until March, which means it will not affect customers during the colder winter months when electricity consumption is generally at its highest." The company said it was investing £120m in the network to improve its resilience and future-proof its systems. It said it continued to focus on managing costs responsibly and driving efficiencies across the business. Follow BBC Jersey on X, external, Facebook, external and Instagram, external. news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, pro-crypto lawmaker Tom Emmer was elected House Republican minority whip as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress, hotter-than-expected US inflation raised concerns about a potential half-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and Coinbase, Kalshi and other trading firms backed the CFTC in a legal battle over perpetual futures tied to US stocks. Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X. Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade.

news.title: Initia confirms second exploit in 3 weeks, $3.27M stolen in latest attack
news.summary: Initia said an attacker exploited compromised cloud credentials to move $3.27 million in crypto assets, with about $2.16 million remaining frozen on its halted network.

news.titleTr: Initia confirms second exploit in 3 weeks, $3.27M stolen in latest attack
news.summaryTr: Initia said an attacker exploited compromised cloud credentials to move $3.27 million in crypto assets, with about $2.16 million remaining frozen on its halted network.
news.articleText: Initia confirms second exploit in 3 weeks, $3.27M stolen in latest attack Initia said an attacker exploited compromised cloud credentials to move $3.27 million in crypto assets, with about $2.16 million remaining frozen on its halted network. Layer-1 blockchain network Initia confirmed Wednesday that it has suffered its second security exploit in less than three weeks, with an attacker stealing about $3.27 million in crypto assets after compromising the platform’s cloud infrastructure. On Wednesday, Initia said the attacker gained unauthorized access on Monday through a command injection attack involving a compromised Google Cloud Platform key. The company said the breach exposed environment variables, allowing the attacker to access Initia’s GitHub and cloud accounts and obtain additional credentials. According to Initia, the attacker accessed Anvil, a platform hosting rollups, and validated fraudulent Inter-Blockchain Communication (IBC) withdrawals from five rollups, releasing assets held in the network’s escrow accounts. Initia said about $2.16 million of the stolen assets remain frozen on its halted network. The attacker sold assets on Initia’s decentralized exchange and withdrew 13,400 TIA, 8,000 USDC.inj and 597,000 Noble USDC. No INIT tokens were withdrawn. Initia halted its layer-1 on Tuesday and said it intends to restore the backing of affected assets. The blockchain said recovery efforts are ongoing with its law enforcement and security partners. The incident follows an Oct. 23 exploit that saw an attacker drain about $2.7 million after exploiting a vulnerability in Initia’s MoveVM script cache. This allowed malicious code to bypass security checks and create unbacked token balances that were subsequently bridged out of the network. Related: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic

news.summary: The cross-chain bridge said a social engineering attack targeting domain registrar Namecheap allowed hackers to redirect users to a phishing site.

news.titleTr: Across Protocol restores website after hackers hijack domain
news.summaryTr: The cross-chain bridge said a social engineering attack targeting domain registrar Namecheap allowed hackers to redirect users to a phishing site.
news.articleText: Across Protocol restores website after hackers hijack domain The cross-chain bridge said a social engineering attack targeting domain registrar Namecheap allowed hackers to redirect users to a phishing site. Cross-chain bridge Across Protocol said it has regained control of its website after a social engineering attack on Tuesday enabled attackers to gain control of its domain, replacing its website with a phishing site. In a post on Wednesday, Across said the across.to domain is back under their control with help from Namecheap founder Richard Kirkendall, and that all systems are now working normally. “All affected users will be made whole. We’ll share a full post-mortem in the coming days,” the team said on X. The update follows Across’s Tuesday warning to users to avoid its app amid reports of drained wallets. The total losses and number of affected users have not yet been disclosed. Across attributes takeover to social engineering In an earlier update, Across said a social engineering attack on its domain registrar, Namecheap, gave an attacker control of its domain at approximately 18:45 UTC. The team said it was alerted within 15 minutes and immediately worked to shut the website down. Security response group SEAL911 helped flag the domain as phishing with major wallets, while Cloudflare marked it as at risk and later removed its DNS records. Some users who visited the domain before the malicious site was fully blocked may have been affected, the team said. Third-party integrations and API users were unaffected. The incident affected one of the largest cross-chain bridges by trading activity. Across ranked third by 30-day transfer volume, behind Circle and LayerZero, according to DefiLlama, having processed about $5.9 billion over the period. Related: Across Protocol warns users to avoid app amid reports of drained wallets

news.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
news.summary: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
news.summaryTr: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.
news.articleText: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave - Published The family of former US President John F Kennedy has sued to block construction of a triumphal arch that President Donald Trump plans to build in the nation's capital. Nine members of the political dynasty argue the 250ft (76m) structure would block the view of Kennedy's grave, as well as the graves of thousands of veterans buried at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia. Last week, a US judge temporarily halted the project on the heels of a vote allowing construction to proceed. The White House said it was "unfortunate" to see that some members of the Kennedy family had joined litigation against an arch "intended to honor our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery". "The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation," White House spokesman Davis R Ingle said in a statement to the BBC. "We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds," he added. Last week the project won approval from the National Capital Planning Commission. But US District Judge Tanya Chutkan then ruled there should be a 14-day pause before any work can start on the arch as litigation plays out. The Kennedy family filed its complaint under a joint lawsuit brought by the state of Virginia and Washington DC seeking to block construction, arguing that the arch will damage "historically significant sightlines" if erected at the gateway of the cemetery. The plaintiffs include seven children of Robert and Ethel Kennedy, as well as their grandson - former Democrat congressman Joe Kennedy - and Ted Kennedy's son Edward Kennedy Jr. It does not include Trump cabinet official Robert F Kennedy Jr, who leads the Department of Health and Human Services. Their motion moves to intervene in two other lawsuits filed by conservationists and veterans seeking to halt the construction. They say the arch would be a "permanent denigration" of the gravesites and that the Kennedy offspring "would never again be able to appreciate both sites as they always have before, and as the Kennedy family always intended". The Kennedy family argues the structure "will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials established in the Kennedy family's honor" at the cemetery. The structure would also "fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites", including the memorials of hundreds of thousands of US veterans, the Kennedys said. The complaint said that the National Park Service and Interior Department authorised construction on 5 November 2026 without the necessary congressional approval. The so-called Arc de Trump is one of the president's efforts to remake the capital city and is meant to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary. Last year, he also added his name to the Kennedy Center, a major Washington DC cultural institution named in honour of JFK. Trump's name remained on the facade for six months until the addition was ruled illegal and removed. Related topics - Published21 May - Published25 September - Published5 days ago

news.titleTr: Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip
news.summaryTr: The Minnesota lawmaker, who helped establish the Congressional Crypto Caucus, will stay on as Republican whip after Democrats won the midterms.
news.articleText: Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip The Minnesota lawmaker, who helped establish the Congressional Crypto Caucus, will stay on as Republican whip after Democrats won the midterms. Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. Emmer has been a leading Republican voice on digital assets. In March 2025, he and Representative Ritchie Torres announced the bipartisan Congressional Crypto Caucus, aimed at mobilizing support for digital asset legislation, including stablecoin and market structure bills. He is also an original cosponsor of the CLARITY Act and introduced the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act, which seeks to clarify that blockchain developers and infrastructure providers who do not control customer funds are not money transmitters under federal law. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X. news.summary: The infamous 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by the El Salvador military which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.

news.titleTr: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
news.summaryTr: The infamous 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by the El Salvador military which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.
news.articleText: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says - Published The headquarters of one of Haiti's largest crime gangs has been destroyed by El Salvador's military, the Salvadoran president has said. The infamous 400 Mawozo gang, which is known for kidnappings and intimidation tactics, was targeted in a ground and air attack at a complex on the outskirts of Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince. It is El Salvador's first military action on a Haitian target since it deployed more than 2,000 soldiers there last month, as part of a mission to rescue four missing Salvadoran technicians. Haiti has been plagued by gang violence for years, with heavily armed groups controlling large parts of the capital, and beyond. El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele announced the news on X, external, boasting that most of the gang members fled without trying to fight. "We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters," he wrote on Tuesday. The post was accompanied by video of several helicopters firing on a large complex, reportedly in the suburb of Croix-des-Bouquets, the gang's stronghold. As the helicopters circle above, dozens of people can be seen running out of the property, fleeing the strikes. Several media outlets have reported that as many as 20 people were killed, however that has not been confirmed by authorities. There has also been no official confirmation of the extent of the damage at the property, with Haitians questioning whether it has been destroyed or just damaged. The Miami Herald reports that the gang's leader, Wilson "Lanmò San Jou" Joseph, was not there at the time. The BBC has not been able to verify the video posted by Bukele, nor whether the property is indeed the gang's headquarters. Haiti's National Police drone task force was involved in the attack, supported by Salvadoran soldiers, the Miami Herald reports, citing several sources. Posting on X after the strikes, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked the Salvadoran military's commitment "in the fight against gangs", and said the two nations would keep working together, along with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), to "regain control of the territory and restore state authority". "THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!" he added. Some 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers were deployed to Haiti last month after four air force technicians were abducted at gunpoint while food shopping in October. El Salvador's right-wing president has vowed to bring the men home alive and warned the gang to release them immediately or face sustained pressure from his military. The four abducted men were working as part of the GSF, made up of troops from several nations, initially led by soldiers from Chad. President Bukele's move to send thousands of Salvadoran troops to Haiti has raised concerns, with critics saying they are not all working within the command structure of the GSF. It has raised questions about the operational legitimacy and legality of their actions in the Caribbean nation. Amnesty International has urged both countries to "ensure all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law". Such concerns do not appear to faze Bukele, however, who continues to directly warn and target the gang leaders. The attack on the supposed gang headquarters seemingly came after a user on X had urged Bukele to attack the complex. "Where is that house? Give us the exact address, and we'll destroy it," he replied to the post, which has now been taken down, apparently for violating X's rules. The 400 Mawozo gang is the largest criminal organisation in Haiti, and known for kidnappings, extortion, murders and arms trafficking. Haiti is the poorest country in the Americas and remains largely under gang control. At least 5,700 people have been killed or injured there by gangs or during operations against them between 1 January and 11 September this year alone, the United Nations has said. El Salvador has recorded huge reductions in gang violence under President Bukele as part of a sweeping crackdown, and he has vowed to do the same in Haiti. However, human rights groups have argued that the way he has done it is unlawful, with the open-ended extension of emergency laws, the treatment of detainees in El Salvador's high-security mega-prison and the mass trials of alleged gang members. Haiti has been plagued by gang violence for years, with heavily armed groups controlling large parts of the capital, and beyond. El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele announced the news on X, external, boasting that most of the gang members fled without trying to fight. "We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters," he wrote on Tuesday. The post was accompanied by video of several helicopters firing on a large complex, reportedly in the suburb of Croix-des-Bouquets, the gang's stronghold. As the helicopters circle above, dozens of people can be seen running out of the property, fleeing the strikes. Several media outlets have reported that as many as 20 people were killed, however that has not been confirmed by authorities. There has also been no official confirmation of the extent of the damage at the property, with Haitians questioning whether it has been destroyed or just damaged. The Miami Herald reports that the gang's leader, Wilson "Lanmò San Jou" Joseph, was not there at the time. The BBC has not been able to verify the video posted by Bukele, nor whether the property is indeed the gang's headquarters. Haiti's National Police drone task force was involved in the attack, supported by Salvadoran soldiers, the Miami Herald reports, citing several sources. Posting on X after the strikes, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked the Salvadoran military's commitment "in the fight against gangs", and said the two nations would keep working together, along with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), to "regain control of the territory and restore state authority". "THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!" he added. Some 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers were deployed to Haiti last month after four air force technicians were abducted at gunpoint while food shopping in October. El Salvador's right-wing president has vowed to bring the men home alive and warned the gang to release them immediately or face sustained pressure from his military. The four abducted men were working as part of the GSF, made up of troops from several nations, initially led by soldiers from Chad. President Bukele's move to send thousands of Salvadoran troops to Haiti has raised concerns, with critics saying they are not all working within the command structure of the GSF. It has raised questions about the operational legitimacy and legality of their actions in the Caribbean nation. Amnesty International has urged both countries to "ensure all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law". Such concerns do not appear to faze Bukele, however, who continues to directly warn and target the gang leaders. The attack on the supposed gang headquarters seemingly came after a user on X had urged Bukele to attack the complex. "Where is that house? Give us the exact address, and we'll destroy it," he replied to the post, which has now been taken down, apparently for violating X's rules. The 400 Mawozo gang is the largest criminal organisation in Haiti, and known for kidnappings, extortion, murders and arms trafficking. Haiti is the poorest country in the Americas and remains largely under gang control. At least 5,700 people have been killed or injured there by gangs or during operations against them between 1 January and 11 September this year alone, the United Nations has said. El Salvador has recorded huge reductions in gang violence under President Bukele as part of a sweeping crackdown, and he has vowed to do the same in Haiti. However, human rights groups have argued that the way he has done it is unlawful, with the open-ended extension of emergency laws, the treatment of detainees in El Salvador's high-security mega-prison and the mass trials of alleged gang members. news.titleTr: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor
news.summaryTr: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
news.articleText: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor - Published Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show. Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device. The BBC has contacted his representatives. Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court". He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician". "Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday. "We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added. Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said. Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material. In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old. Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention. He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ. FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions". Markle has called the allegations "sick lies". He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated. The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed." She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children". Related topics - Published29 October

news.title: Judge allows Trump's $10bn defamation case against BBC to proceed
news.summary: But the court dismisses the other part of Trump's lawsuit that alleged the BBC had violated a Florida law.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Judge allows Trump's $10bn defamation case against BBC to proceed
news.summaryTr: But the court dismisses the other part of Trump's lawsuit that alleged the BBC had violated a Florida law.
news.articleText: Judge allows Trump's $10bn defamation case against BBC to proceed - Published A federal judge in Florida has allowed US President Donald Trump's defamation case against the BBC to go ahead after the broadcaster sought to dismiss it. But Judge Jeffrey Kuntz dismissed a second claim in the $10bn (£7.5bn) lawsuit under the state's unfair trade practices law. The US president is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021. Trump called the judge's ruling a "huge victory" in a Truth Social post on Tuesday. A BBC spokesperson said: "We are surprised by this decision but respect the Court's authority and note the case will now proceed to the next stage." The BBC spokesperson added: "We remain confident in our position and will continue to respond through the proper legal process." Judge Kuntz found Trump's defamation allegations against the BBC sufficient for the case to continue, although he did not make a ruling on the merits of the case. "Whether President Trump can prove these claims and establish he sustained damages at summary judgment or trial is left for another day," he wrote in Tuesday's order. Trump's lawsuit - filed in Florida - accuses the BBC of "intentionally, maliciously and deceptively doctoring" the speech he gave outside the Capitol on 6 January 2021. The BBC apologised and said that the broadcast had given "the mistaken impression that Trump made a direct call for violent action". The broadcaster has since asked that the court dismiss the lawsuit, arguing the programme does not meet the legal criteria for defamation and was not available in the US. Along with defamation, Trump claimed in the lawsuit that the broadcaster had violated Florida law, specifically the Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act. Kuntz on Tuesday dismissed that part of the lawsuit, ruling that the documentary did not constitute commercial speech. - Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit - Published23 October A judge ordered Trump last month to answer questions under oath in the lawsuit by 11 December, after the president cancelled a previous deposition last month, citing "matters of national importance". A lawyer representing the BBC said in court that Trump was campaigning in Georgia in October on the scheduled day and had "prioritised that" over answering their questions. Earlier this year, Trump's lawyers conceded they had no evidence that the documentary was available in the US on the BBC's BritBox subscription service - as they originally argued - or on the BBC's website, BBC Select or through US broadcasters. Trump ultimately agreed to drop BBC Studios, the broadcaster's commercial arm, from his defamation lawsuit, after the BBC argued that it had "no role in creating or producing the documentary". news.title: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
news.summary: The project warned that installations running older versions were vulnerable and urged operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
news.summaryTr: The project warned that installations running older versions were vulnerable and urged operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading.
news.articleText: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts The project warned that installations running older versions were vulnerable and urged operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading. Bitcoin Lightning wallet platform LNbits has urged users to update immediately to its latest version after reporting a wave of attacks targeting LNbits instances that resulted in stolen funds. The project published version 1.7.0 on Tuesday, describing it as a critical release addressing vulnerabilities and strengthening authentication, extension management and payment handling. LNbits warned that updating alone would not protect installations whose credentials had already been compromised. “It’s been a very challenging few days, working relentlessly to get the v1.7 release out after our users and we suffered losses,” LNbits creator Ben Arc said on X. LNbits provides software for running Bitcoin Lightning wallets and payment applications, including merchant checkouts, tipping services and paywalls. Developer Ben Arc said in May that about 200,000 people run the software themselves. LNbits first warned operators on Sunday to disable its Paywall extension while it investigated a potential vulnerability. Just over an hour later, the project urged users to shut down their LNbits servers immediately, citing a wave of attacks. It also took its own hosted installations offline. The company has not yet detailed the exploit and how many were impacted by it. In an announcement accompanying the emergency patch, LNbits said the vulnerability affects all versions before 1.7.0 and puts funds at risk of theft. Related: BitMart founder says security team ‘severely understaffed’ after new hack It also warned that credentials exposed before upgrading could still give attackers access afterward, urging operators to reset wallet keys, replace funding-source credentials and treat secrets stored in LNbits settings as compromised and recommended moving to a fresh server if a compromise is suspected. Cointelegraph reached out to Ben Arc and LNbits for comment. One user, Kevin Ravensberg, said attackers exploited his LNbits instance, withdrawing about 2.3 million satoshis, or 0.023 Bitcoin, through newly created accounts before he could shut down the server. The company said a separate report detailing the exploit would follow. Magazine: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss

news.title: CFTC warns Kalshi of imminent charges over notification of contracts: Politico
news.summary: The prediction markets operator says the issue involves procedural errors affecting a handful of contracts, many of which weren’t live, according to Politico.

news.titleTr: CFTC warns Kalshi of imminent charges over notification of contracts: Politico
news.summaryTr: The prediction markets operator says the issue involves procedural errors affecting a handful of contracts, many of which weren’t live, according to Politico.
news.articleText: CFTC warns Kalshi of imminent charges over notification of contracts: Politico The prediction markets operator says the issue involves procedural errors affecting a handful of contracts, many of which weren’t live, according to Politico. Prediction markets operator Kalshi is being warned of imminent charges from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission over whether the operator properly notified the agency about new products, Politico reported Tuesday. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating notifications involving dozens of products, the report said, citing a person with direct knowledge of the probe. The agency’s private notification to Kalshi suggests that charges could follow. The investigation has been underway for months, the person said. Speaking to Politico, Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana described the matter as a procedural error involving submissions for a handful of contracts, many of which never went live. “We are already addressing the issue,” she added. The potential enforcement action comes as the CFTC fights to establish its exclusive authority over prediction markets, including by challenging state efforts to regulate Kalshi. Separately, Kalshi is backing the regulator in a separate legal battle over its authority. On Monday, the company joined Coinbase and four other firms in seeking permission to file a brief supporting the CFTC’s treatment of perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. Related: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-
